_meta.name: Occupational Churn
_meta.unit: dissimilarity index, percentage-point shift in the occupational mix over the prior 12 months, 12-month moving average
_meta.source: Yale Budget Lab, Tracking the Impact of AI on the Labor Market (from CPS microdata)
_meta.note: A Duncan dissimilarity index of how much the occupational composition of the US labor force has shifted against a rolling 12-month baseline, computed from monthly Current Population Survey microdata by the Yale Budget Lab and updated with each CPS release (repository data file, all sectors, rolling variant). The Budget Lab's reading as of July 2026 CPS: churn "remains flat, lies within historical ranges, or continues along pre-AI trends." A rise would mean the mix of jobs is changing faster; it does not say why. Begins January 2022; October 2025 CPS is missing (federal shutdown).
